core_claims.title: Product cycle driven by new form factors
core_claims.statement: The introduction of the foldable iPhone Duo and Siri AI rollout may support product revenue growth into FY2027, but evidence for upgrade cycle extension is missing
core_claims.why_core: New product cycles are a key driver of hardware revenue growth and can shift the earnings trajectory.
core_claims.reconciliation_reason: direct complete support with required source relationship

support_evidence.fact: Apple introduced iPhone Duo, its first foldable iPhone, with a 7.6-inch inner display and a 5.4-inch outer display.
support_evidence.excerpt: Apple today introduced iPhone Duo, the first foldable iPhone. Opened, it is the thinnest iPhone ever, with a 7.6-inch inner display
support_evidence.reason: Primary source confirms the launch of the foldable iPhone Duo, a key new form factor that could drive demand.
support_evidence.proves: Apple introduced a foldable iPhone with specific display sizes.
support_evidence.does_not_prove: It does not prove that this product will extend the upgrade cycle or increase revenue.

support_evidence.fact: Apple's software updates including Siri AI started rolling out on September 14, 2026 across iOS 27, iPadOS 27, and macOS 27.
support_evidence.excerpt: Siri AI, the next generation of Apple Intelligence, powerful parental controls, and an expansive set of software improvements start rolling out today across iOS 27, iPadOS 27, macOS 27, and other Apple platforms
support_evidence.reason: Primary source confirms the rollout of Siri AI across Apple platforms, a software feature that could enhance device appeal.
support_evidence.proves: Siri AI started rolling out on September 14, 2026.
support_evidence.does_not_prove: It does not prove that Siri AI will drive upgrade cycle extension or revenue growth.

support_evidence.fact: Apple launched the Duo, a folding iPhone priced at $1,999, on September 9, 2026.
support_evidence.excerpt: Apple (AAPL.O), opens new tab on Wednesday redefined its flagship smartphone with the launch of the Duo, a folding $1,999 iPhone
support_evidence.reason: Independent media confirms the launch and pricing of the foldable iPhone Duo, validating the product introduction.
support_evidence.proves: Apple launched the Duo, a folding iPhone priced at $1,999, on September 9, 2026.
support_evidence.does_not_prove: It does not prove that the product will extend the upgrade cycle or support revenue growth.

counter_evidence.fact: TSMC's 3nm, 2nm, and CoWoS advanced packaging capacity remained in short supply in late Q3 2026, prompting the foundry to adjust advanced capacity allocation amid major customer order changes.
counter_evidence.excerpt: TSMC's 3nm, 2nm, and CoWoS advanced packaging capacity remained in short supply in late 2026's third quarter, as changes in major customer orders and front-end and back-end supply models prompted the foundry to adjust its advanced capacity
counter_evidence.reason: TSMC advanced packaging capacity shortage and order changes could constrain supply of new iPhones, potentially limiting revenue growth.
counter_evidence.proves: TSMC's advanced capacity was in short supply and adjusted due to major customer order changes.
counter_evidence.does_not_prove: It does not directly prove that Apple's iPhone Duo or Siri AI will fail to drive growth; it only indicates potential supply constraints.

missing_evidence: Direct evidence of iPhone upgrade cycle duration or consumer upgrade rates following the launch of Duo and Siri AI.
Revenue forecasts or sales data for the Duo and Siri AI-enabled devices.
Independent analysis of consumer demand and pre-order volumes for the Duo.
Evidence on the impact of Siri AI on device upgrade decisions.

candidates.statement: Services revenue growth is structurally supported by an expanding installed base and recurring monetization, making it more durable than cyclical hardware revenue.
candidates.why_core: Services is the highest-margin, most recurring revenue stream and a key driver of earnings durability.

candidates.why_core: Supply constraints are a near-term swing factor for revenue and can affect quarterly results.
